Title: Agent Harness (Microsoft Agent Framework)
Key takeaway: Batteries-included harness: chat client -> chat pipeline (function loop, per-call history persistence, compaction) -> context providers (instructions, tools, memory, todos, plan/execute modes, skills) -> middleware (approvals, OTel, bounded looping) -> UX.
Implication for our harness: Closest published reference architecture to what we are building; use its capability matrix as a checklist.

Title: What is an AI Agent Harness?
Key takeaway: Agent = model + harness; harness supplies tools, memory, workspace, guardrails and the reason-act-observe loop. Many production failures (context rot, tool overload, weak verification) are harness failures.
Implication for our harness: Frames harness quality as a first-order performance lever.

Title: Loop Engineering, Harness Engineering, Context Engineering: what's the difference?
Key takeaway: Three layers: context (what the model sees), harness (tools, skills, MCP, hooks, sandboxes; guides + sensors), loop (repeated triggering and verification without a human). Weak lower layers get amplified by loops.
Implication for our harness: Use the three layers as the top-level architecture of the repo.

Title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
Key takeaway: Context is a finite attention budget: find the smallest set of high-signal tokens. Techniques: just-in-time retrieval via tools, compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agent isolation.
Implication for our harness: Make the context assembler a first-class module with explicit token budgets per section.

Title: Managing context on the Claude Developer Platform (context editing + memory tool)
Key takeaway: Context editing auto-clears stale tool results; memory tool is a client-side file store. Internal agentic-search eval: +39% with both, +29% with editing alone.
Implication for our harness: Implement tool-result clearing + a file-backed memory tool; both are provider-independent ideas.

Title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
Key takeaway: Initializer agent writes feature list, progress file, init script and first commit; later sessions read those artifacts and work one feature at a time.
Implication for our harness: Persist session state as plain artifacts (progress.md, features.json, git) not only as chat history.

Title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
Key takeaway: KV-cache hit rate is the key production metric; keep prefix stable and context append-only; mask tools instead of removing; file system as memory; recite goals (todo.md); keep errors in context.
Implication for our harness: Design prompt layout for cache stability; deterministic serialization; never reorder tools mid-session.

Title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
Key takeaway: 18 models degrade non-uniformly as input grows, even on simple tasks; needle-in-a-haystack overstates long-context ability; distractors and low query similarity accelerate decay.
Implication for our harness: Do not treat a large window as free; compact early and keep context lean.

Title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
Key takeaway: Accuracy is highest when relevant info is at the start or end of context and drops in the middle.
Implication for our harness: Put instructions and critical state at the edges (system prompt + latest turn).

Title: Context Engineering for Agents (write / select / compress / isolate)
Key takeaway: Taxonomy of context strategies: write (scratchpads, memory), select (retrieval), compress (summaries, trimming), isolate (sub-agents, sandboxes, state).
Implication for our harness: Use the four verbs as the module boundaries of the context subsystem.

Title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
Key takeaway: OS-style virtual memory: in-context 'core' memory plus paged external memory, managed by the model through self-editing memory tools.
Implication for our harness: Model memory as tiers (core / recall / archival) with tools for the agent to edit them.

Title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
Key takeaway: Pre-compute over context while idle so test-time compute drops (~5x less for similar accuracy on their stateful benchmarks).
Implication for our harness: Background 'consolidation' job between sessions: summarise, index, update memory blocks.

Title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
Key takeaway: Extract-consolidate-retrieve memory pipeline (+graph variant); on LOCOMO reports 91% lower p95 latency and >90% token savings vs full context.
Implication for our harness: Benchmark candidate memory backend; copy the ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP consolidation step.

Title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
Key takeaway: Bi-temporal knowledge graph (Graphiti) with episode, entity and community subgraphs; tracks when facts were true vs ingested.
Implication for our harness: If memory must handle changing facts, store validity intervals, not just embeddings.

Title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
Key takeaway: Zettelkasten-style memory: notes with links that evolve as new memories arrive.
Implication for our harness: Consider linked notes over flat vector store for long-lived project memory.

Title: Agentic Context Engineering (ACE): Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving LMs
Org / Authors: Zhang et al. (Stanford, SambaNova, UC Berkeley)
Key takeaway: Contexts as growing 'playbooks' via generate-reflect-curate with incremental delta updates; avoids brevity bias and context collapse. +10.6% agents, +8.6% finance.
Implication for our harness: Never let an LLM rewrite the whole memory/playbook; apply itemised deltas.

Title: Recursive Language Models
Key takeaway: Put the long prompt in a REPL variable; the model inspects/splits it with code and recursively calls sub-LLMs. Handles inputs ~100x beyond the window.
Implication for our harness: Offer a 'context as variable' tool path for huge inputs instead of stuffing the window.

Title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
Key takeaway: Memory stream + reflection; retrieval scored by recency, importance and relevance.
Implication for our harness: Use a combined recency/importance/relevance score for memory retrieval.

Title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval
Key takeaway: Prepend chunk-specific context before embedding + BM25; reported 49% fewer retrieval failures (67% with reranking).
Implication for our harness: Default RAG recipe for codebase/doc search: contextual embeddings + BM25 + rerank.

Title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference
Key takeaway: Small LM drops low-information tokens; up to 20x compression with small loss. LLMLingua-2 treats it as token classification.
Implication for our harness: Optional compressor stage for bulky tool output (logs, HTML) before it enters context.

Title: Claude Code memory (CLAUDE.md hierarchy)
Key takeaway: Hierarchical instruction files (enterprise / user / project / local) loaded at start; imports supported.
Implication for our harness: Support layered instruction files and also read AGENTS.md for portability.

Title: Organizing Context in a Multi-Agent Harness
Key takeaway: Subagent context modes: 'isolated' (task only) vs 'fork' (inherits supervisor conversation, reuses prompt cache). Fork for workers/memory agents; isolate for verifiers, reviewers, parallel researchers.
Implication for our harness: Make fork vs isolated an explicit per-subagent setting.

Title: Migrate to the Responses API
Key takeaway: Responses returns typed output Items, supports server-side state (previous_response_id / Conversations) and persists reasoning across tool calls; recommended for new projects.
Implication for our harness: Internal message model must be item-based (text, tool_call, tool_result, reasoning) not just role/content strings.

Title: OpenAI SDK compatibility
Key takeaway: Claude reachable through the OpenAI SDK for testing, but many features (caching, thinking details, some tool features) need the native API.
Implication for our harness: Use native adapters per provider; treat OpenAI-compatible endpoints as a fallback tier.

Title: OpenAI compatibility for the Gemini API
Key takeaway: Gemini callable via OpenAI client libraries with some feature gaps.
Implication for our harness: Same as LLM-02: compat layer is convenient but lossy.

Title: LiteLLM (SDK + AI Gateway)
Key takeaway: OpenAI-format interface to 100+ providers; Router with retries, fallbacks, load-balancing; proxy adds virtual keys, budgets, logging.
Implication for our harness: Candidate to wrap rather than build; or copy its router semantics (fallbacks, cooldowns).

Title: OpenRouter provider routing
Key takeaway: Per-request 'models' fallback list and 'provider' object (order, allow_fallbacks, price/latency sort).
Implication for our harness: Expose ordered fallback chains + provider pinning in our config schema.

Title: Introducing any-llm: a unified API to access any LLM provider
Key takeaway: Thin unified interface that delegates to each vendor's official SDK; no proxy required.
Implication for our harness: Prefer official SDKs underneath our adapter layer for fidelity.

Title: AI SDK (provider abstraction for TypeScript)
Key takeaway: Unified generateText/streamText/tool APIs over many providers; provider registry and middleware.
Implication for our harness: Reference design if the harness is TypeScript.

Title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
Org / Authors: Ong et al. (LMSYS, UC Berkeley, Anyscale)
Key takeaway: Router trained on Chatbot Arena preferences picks strong vs weak model; >2x cost savings with small quality loss.
Implication for our harness: Add a routing hook (cheap vs strong model) that can start rule-based and later be learned.

Title: FrugalGPT: How to Use LLMs While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
Key takeaway: Prompt adaptation, LLM approximation (caching) and cascades; up to 98% cost cut at equal quality.
Implication for our harness: Cascade pattern: try cheap model, escalate on low confidence / failed verification.

Title: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server
Key takeaway: Self-hosted open models behind an OpenAI-style endpoint.
Implication for our harness: Local/self-hosted provider tier through the same adapter.

Title: Prompt caching (Claude)
Key takeaway: Explicit cache_control breakpoints; cached reads billed at a fraction of input price; order is tools -> system -> messages.
Implication for our harness: Stable-prefix layout + cache breakpoints on tools/system/long docs; track cache hit rate.

Title: Prompt caching (OpenAI)
Key takeaway: Automatic prefix caching for long prompts; prompt_cache_key improves routing to cached shards.
Implication for our harness: Same layout discipline works across providers.

Title: Context caching (Gemini)
Key takeaway: Implicit and explicit caching with TTLs.
Implication for our harness: Adapter must expose provider caching knobs uniformly.

Title: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
Key takeaway: Paged KV cache removes fragmentation, enabling high-throughput batching and prefix sharing.
Implication for our harness: Relevant if we self-host; explains why shared prefixes are cheap.

Title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured LM Programs (RadixAttention)
Key takeaway: Radix-tree KV-cache reuse across calls + compressed FSM constrained decoding; up to 6.4x throughput.
Implication for our harness: Branching agent calls that share prefixes are cheap on such runtimes; design for prefix sharing.

Title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
Key takeaway: Draft model proposes tokens, target verifies; 2-3x speedup with identical output distribution.
Implication for our harness: Provider-side; matters for self-hosting and for choosing 'fast' endpoints.

Title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
Key takeaway: Feature-level drafting; ~2.7-3.5x latency speedup; successors EAGLE-2/3.
Implication for our harness: Self-hosting only.

Title: Medusa: LLM Inference Acceleration with Multiple Decoding Heads
Key takeaway: Extra decoding heads predict several future tokens; no separate draft model.
Implication for our harness: Self-hosting only.

Title: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling (LLMCompiler)
Key takeaway: Planner builds a DAG of tool calls, executor runs independent ones in parallel; up to 3.7x latency and 6.7x cost improvement vs ReAct.
Implication for our harness: Execute independent tool calls concurrently; allow the model to emit parallel calls.

Title: Skeleton-of-Thought: Prompting LLMs for Efficient Parallel Generation
Key takeaway: Generate an outline then expand points in parallel for lower wall-clock latency.
Implication for our harness: Pattern for long-form generation tasks (reports, docs).

Title: Message Batches API
Key takeaway: Async batch processing at reduced price for non-interactive work.
Implication for our harness: Route evals and background jobs (memory consolidation, indexing) to batch tier.

Title: Batch API
Key takeaway: 24h async batch jobs at discounted price.
Implication for our harness: Same as PERF-11.

Title: Predicted Outputs
Key takeaway: Supply expected output (e.g. the file being edited) to cut latency on regenerations.
Implication for our harness: Speeds up whole-file rewrites; prefer diff/patch edits anyway.

Title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative LM Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
Key takeaway: Programs declare signatures/modules; optimizers compile prompts and few-shot demos against a metric.
Implication for our harness: Separate prompt *content* from code so it can be optimised against evals.

Title: Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage LM Programs (MIPRO)
Key takeaway: Jointly optimise instructions and demos per module with Bayesian search; up to +13%. Basis of DSPy MIPROv2.
Implication for our harness: Use for optimising sub-agent prompts once we have eval sets.

Title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
Org / Authors: Agrawal et al. (UC Berkeley, Stanford, Databricks)
Key takeaway: Reflects on execution traces in natural language and keeps a Pareto front of prompts; beats GRPO by ~6% avg with up to 35x fewer rollouts; beats MIPROv2 by >10%.
Implication for our harness: Best current candidate for an offline 'optimise this skill/agent prompt' command using our traces.

Title: Large Language Models as Optimizers (OPRO)
Key takeaway: Meta-prompt with past prompts and scores; LLM proposes better ones. Up to +8% GSM8K, +50% BBH over human prompts.
Implication for our harness: Simple baseline optimiser.

Title: TextGrad: Automatic 'Differentiation' via Text
Key takeaway: LLM critiques act as textual gradients propagated through a compound system.
Implication for our harness: Pattern for optimising multi-component pipelines.

Title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers (APE)
Key takeaway: LLM generates and selects instructions by score.
Implication for our harness: Historical baseline.

Title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
Key takeaway: Evolves task prompts and the mutation prompts themselves.
Implication for our harness: Optional evolutionary optimiser idea.

Title: The Prompt Report: A Systematic Survey of Prompt Engineering Techniques
Key takeaway: Taxonomy of 58 text prompting techniques and vocabulary.
Implication for our harness: Reference for prompt library design.

Title: Prompting best practices for Claude 4.x models
Key takeaway: Be explicit, give context/motivation, use XML structure, control verbosity and parallel tool use, state-tracking for long tasks.
Implication for our harness: Per-model prompt variants: harness should allow model-family-specific system prompt fragments.

Title: GPT-5 prompting guide
Key takeaway: Control 'agentic eagerness', tool preambles, reasoning_effort; avoid contradictory instructions (model is very literal); use Responses API to persist reasoning.
Implication for our harness: Same: prompt fragments per model family; expose reasoning-effort knob in config.

Title: Prompt design strategies (Gemini)
Key takeaway: Google's guidance on instructions, few-shot, structure.
Implication for our harness: Input to per-model prompt variants.

Title: What is Prompt Optimization?
Key takeaway: Optimisation = iteratively testing an existing prompt against metrics (vs designing from scratch); templates, few-shot + CoT, meta-prompting, iterative eval.
Implication for our harness: Intro-level; confirms eval-driven loop.

Title: Exploring Prompt Optimization
Key takeaway: Compared few-shot, meta-prompting, meta-prompting+reflection, prompt gradients, evolutionary. Big gains where model lacks domain rules (up to ~200%), little on reasoning; overfitting risk -> hold-out split.
Implication for our harness: Optimise only with a held-out test split; expect gains on rule/knowledge gaps, not raw reasoning.

Title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
Key takeaway: Skill = folder with SKILL.md (name + description frontmatter) plus scripts/resources; progressive disclosure: only metadata is in context until the skill is triggered.
Implication for our harness: Adopt SKILL.md as the native skill format; load metadata at start, body on demand.

Title: Agent Skills specification (open standard)
Key takeaway: Open, vendor-neutral spec for SKILL.md skills; adopted by Codex and many coding agents.
Implication for our harness: Implement spec-compliant loader so skills port across harnesses and models.

Title: Agent Skills (open standard commentary)
Key takeaway: Notes on the standard launch and cross-vendor adoption (OpenAI Codex docs later added skills).
Implication for our harness: Confirms portability is real, not Claude-only.

Title: Codex skills
Key takeaway: OpenAI Codex support for SKILL.md skills.
Implication for our harness: Cross-check differences in discovery paths/metadata vs Claude.

Title: anthropics/skills (example skills repo)
Key takeaway: Reference skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx, skill-creator, etc.).
Implication for our harness: Test corpus for our skill loader.

Title: Claude Code skills docs
Key takeaway: Discovery locations (user, project, plugin), invocation, allowed-tools.
Implication for our harness: Mirror discovery precedence rules.

Title: AGENTS.md
Key takeaway: Plain markdown file of project instructions for coding agents; adopted by 60k+ repos and most coding agents.
Implication for our harness: Read AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md) as project guidance; model-agnostic.

Title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
Org / Authors: Wang et al. (NVIDIA, Caltech et al.)
Key takeaway: Agent writes verified code skills into a retrievable library and composes them later.
Implication for our harness: Skill self-authoring: let the agent propose new skills from successful trajectories (with review).

Title: Model Context Protocol specification (2025-11-25)
Key takeaway: JSON-RPC protocol: tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation; streamable HTTP + stdio; OAuth-based auth.
Implication for our harness: Harness must be a full MCP client (stdio + HTTP, auth, list_changed).

Title: MCP 2025-11-25 changelog
Key takeaway: Experimental Tasks (call-now/fetch-later), OIDC discovery, incremental scope consent, Client ID Metadata Documents. Tasks later moving to an extension.
Implication for our harness: Track spec churn; isolate protocol version handling.

Title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient agents
Key takeaway: Present MCP servers as code APIs in a sandbox; agent loads only needed tools and filters data before it reaches the model (example: 150k -> 2k tokens).
Implication for our harness: Offer a code-execution mode for heavy tool use; needs sandboxing.

Title: Introducing advanced tool use (Tool Search, Programmatic Tool Calling, Tool Use Examples)
Key takeaway: Deferred tool loading via search (Opus 4.5 79.5% -> 88.1% on MCP evals); tools called from code; example calls in tool definitions.
Implication for our harness: Implement deferred tool loading + tool search natively so it works with any model.

Title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
Key takeaway: Fewer, higher-level tools; clear namespacing; token-efficient, meaningful responses; actionable errors; evaluate tools with agents.
Implication for our harness: Tool design guidelines for built-in tools and a lint for MCP tool descriptions.

Title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP
Key takeaway: Convert MCP tools to a TypeScript API and let the model write code against it in an isolate.
Implication for our harness: Independent confirmation of MCP-03.

Title: Linux Foundation announces the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
Key takeaway: MCP, goose and AGENTS.md donated to neutral foundation; members include AWS, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI.
Implication for our harness: MCP is now the vendor-neutral default; low lock-in risk.

Title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
Key takeaway: Agent-to-agent protocol with Agent Cards for discovery; complements MCP (agent<->tool).
Implication for our harness: Optional: expose harness agents via A2A for remote delegation.

Title: A2A protocol specification
Key takeaway: Spec, SDKs and Agent Card schema.
Implication for our harness: Reference if implementing remote agents.

Title: MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks
Key takeaway: Hidden instructions in tool descriptions can exfiltrate files; cross-server shadowing; rug pulls after approval.
Implication for our harness: Pin/hash tool definitions, show full descriptions, warn on changes.

Title: Customize Claude Code with plugins
Key takeaway: Plugin = bundle of slash commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP servers; marketplaces are git repos with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Implication for our harness: Plugin packaging format and marketplace-as-git-repo distribution model.

Title: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
Key takeaway: Open protocol connecting coding agents to editors (Zed, JetBrains, etc.); Gemini CLI and Claude Code (via adapter) supported.
Implication for our harness: Implement ACP server so any editor can drive the harness.

Title: MCP Registry
Key takeaway: Official metadata registry for public MCP servers.
Implication for our harness: Source for an in-harness 'install MCP server' browser.

Title: Apps SDK (built on MCP)
Key takeaway: ChatGPT apps defined as MCP servers with UI resources.
Implication for our harness: Shows MCP extending to UI; watch MCP Apps / UI extensions.

Title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
Key takeaway: Agent writes reflections on failures (from tests/env signals) into episodic memory for the next attempt; 91% HumanEval pass@1.
Implication for our harness: Retry loops should carry a written reflection, not just the error.

Title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
Key takeaway: Generate -> self-critique -> refine loop improves many tasks.
Implication for our harness: Cheap refine pass for style/format tasks.

Title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
Key takeaway: Without external feedback, self-correction often fails or degrades accuracy.
Implication for our harness: Ground feedback in external signals (tests, linters, tools, separate judge) - not 'are you sure?'.

Title: CRITIC: LLMs Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
Key takeaway: Verification through tools (search, code execution) makes self-correction work.
Implication for our harness: Verifier tools are the feedback channel.

Title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
Key takeaway: Principles ('constitution') used for AI critique and revision.
Implication for our harness: Encode project rules as a checkable rubric for judge/reviewer agents.

Title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
Key takeaway: Strong LLM judges reach ~80% agreement with humans; biases: position, verbosity, self-enhancement.
Implication for our harness: When using LLM judges: randomise order, use rubrics, prefer different model family.

Title: Let's Verify Step by Step
Key takeaway: Process supervision (step-level feedback) beats outcome supervision for math reasoning.
Implication for our harness: Check intermediate steps (plans, diffs) not only final output.

Title: Harness design for long-running application development
Key takeaway: Planner / generator / evaluator; a separate skeptical evaluator (driving the app with Playwright) beats self-critique; context resets over compaction for 'context anxiety'.
Implication for our harness: Ship a built-in evaluator role that tests real output, with graded criteria.

Title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
Key takeaway: ~1M-line product built by Codex agents; humans design environments; structural tests and custom linter messages feed remediation instructions back to the agent.
Implication for our harness: Make linters/tests emit agent-readable fix instructions; treat docs/AGENTS.md as a map, not a manual.

Title: Hooks reference (Claude Code)
Key takeaway: Deterministic shell hooks on lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit...) that can block, modify or inject context.
Implication for our harness: Core extension point: deterministic guidance that does not rely on the model remembering rules.

Title: The 'think' tool: enabling Claude to stop and think
Key takeaway: A no-op tool for mid-trajectory reasoning improved policy-heavy tau-bench tasks; works best with examples in prompt.
Implication for our harness: Provide a scratchpad/think tool for models without native interleaved thinking.

Title: Guardrails (OpenAI Agents SDK)
Key takeaway: Input/output guardrails run in parallel with the agent and can trip a wire to halt.
Implication for our harness: Pattern: cheap parallel validators with tripwires.

Title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
Key takeaway: Grade outcomes (environment state) not transcripts; code, model and human graders; capability vs regression evals; pass^k for reliability.
Implication for our harness: Build an eval runner into the harness from day one.

Title: Harness Engineering for Coding Agent Users
Key takeaway: Guides (feedforward) + sensors (feedback); computational (tests, linters, types) vs inferential (LLM review) controls; keep quality left; behaviour harnesses still unsolved.
Implication for our harness: Classify every guidance mechanism as guide/sensor x computational/inferential; prefer computational.

Title: Building effective agents
Key takeaway: Workflows vs agents; patterns: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer; start simple; invest in the agent-computer interface.
Implication for our harness: Foundational vocabulary for the harness's orchestration layer.

Title: How we built our multi-agent research system
Key takeaway: Orchestrator + parallel subagents: +90.2% over single agent on internal research eval but ~15x tokens; token usage explains most variance; detailed delegation briefs matter.
Implication for our harness: Use multi-agent for breadth-first, parallelizable tasks; require structured task briefs.

Title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
Key takeaway: Share full context/traces; actions carry implicit decisions, so parallel writers conflict. Prefer single-threaded agents with context compression.
Implication for our harness: Subagents should be read-mostly / research; one writer per artifact.

Title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
Key takeaway: 14 failure modes in 3 groups: specification/system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification.
Implication for our harness: Checklist for delegation design and for our trace analyser.

Title: A practical guide to building agents
Key takeaway: Model + tools + instructions; single-agent first; manager (agents-as-tools) vs decentralized (handoffs) patterns; layered guardrails; human intervention points.
Implication for our harness: Support both agents-as-tools and handoffs in the delegation API.

Title: OpenAI Agents SDK
Key takeaway: Primitives: agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing.
Implication for our harness: Reference API design; tracing model.

Title: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK
Key takeaway: Agent loop: gather context -> take action -> verify work -> repeat; file system as context; subagents; compaction.
Implication for our harness: Our core loop should make the verify step explicit.

Title: Subagents (Claude Code)
Key takeaway: Markdown-defined agents with own system prompt, tool allowlist and model; isolated context.
Implication for our harness: Agent definition format: frontmatter (name, description, tools, model) + prompt body.

Title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
Key takeaway: 16 parallel agents, no orchestrator, shared repo with lock files and tests as coordination; ~2,000 sessions, ~$20k, 100k-line Rust compiler.
Implication for our harness: Tests + git + lightweight locking can coordinate many agents; good harness stress test.

Title: Unrolling the Codex agent loop
Key takeaway: How Codex CLI assembles prompts, calls Responses API, appends tool output, manages context/compaction and caching.
Implication for our harness: Closest public description of a production harness loop; compare with ours.

Title: Agent Development Kit (ADK)
Key takeaway: Sequential/parallel/loop workflow agents + LLM agents; sessions, state, memory; A2A support; Python/Java/Go/TS.
Implication for our harness: Reference for deterministic workflow agents mixed with LLM agents.

Title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
Key takeaway: Interleave reasoning traces with actions; base pattern of tool-using agents.
Implication for our harness: Background.

Title: AutoGen: Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
Key takeaway: Conversable agents and group chat as a programming model.
Implication for our harness: Background on conversation-based orchestration.

Title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
Key takeaway: SOP-driven roles exchanging structured documents instead of free chat.
Implication for our harness: Delegation via structured artifacts (specs, plans) reduces drift.

Title: LangGraph
Key takeaway: Graph-based agent orchestration with checkpointing, human-in-the-loop interrupts, durable execution.
Implication for our harness: Reference for checkpoint/resume and interrupts.

Title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents
Key takeaway: Private data + untrusted content + external communication in one agent = exfiltration risk via prompt injection.
Implication for our harness: Permission engine should detect and block trifecta combinations per session.

Title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
Key takeaway: Privileged planner + quarantined LLM for untrusted data + capability/provenance tracking interpreter.
Implication for our harness: Taint-track untrusted tool output; restrict what tainted data can flow into.

Title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
Key takeaway: Six patterns: action-selector, plan-then-execute, map-reduce, dual LLM, code-then-execute, context-minimization.
Implication for our harness: Menu of architectural defences to offer as harness modes.

Title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous (sandboxing)
Key takeaway: OS-level filesystem + network isolation for bash; cut permission prompts by 84% internally.
Implication for our harness: Sandbox first, then auto-approve inside the sandbox; prompts only for boundary crossings.

Title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
Key takeaway: ASI01-ASI10: goal hijack, tool misuse, identity/privilege, supply chain, code execution, memory poisoning, inter-agent comms, cascading failures, human trust, rogue agents.
Implication for our harness: Threat-model checklist for the harness.

Title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025)
Key takeaway: Prompt injection, sensitive info disclosure, supply chain, excessive agency, etc.
Implication for our harness: Baseline threat model.

Title: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for GenAI agent spans
Key takeaway: Standard span names/attributes: invoke_agent, create_agent, chat, execute_tool; gen_ai.* attributes; MCP conventions; still in development.
Implication for our harness: Emit OTel GenAI spans so any backend (Langfuse, Phoenix, Datadog...) can show traces.

Title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
Key takeaway: Interface design (windowed file viewer, linted edits, concise search output) drives agent performance.
Implication for our harness: Invest in tool ergonomics (ACI) as much as prompts.

Title: SWE-bench: Can LMs Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
Key takeaway: Standard coding-agent benchmark (Verified subset widely used).
Implication for our harness: External benchmark for harness regression tracking.

Title: tau-bench: Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
Key takeaway: Simulated user + domain APIs + policies; introduces pass^k reliability metric. Successor tau2-bench.
Implication for our harness: Use pass^k for reliability; good model for conversational agent evals.

Title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic CLI Tasks
Key takeaway: 89 hard terminal tasks (TB 2.0) run via the Harbor harness; same model scores very differently across harnesses.
Implication for our harness: Primary external benchmark for a terminal harness; integrate Harbor adapter.

Title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
Key takeaway: 50%-success task horizon has doubled about every 7 months.
Implication for our harness: Design for multi-hour autonomous sessions: durability, checkpoints, resumability.

Title: AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction Protocol)
Key takeaway: Event-stream protocol between agent backends and front-end UIs.
Implication for our harness: If we build a GUI/web front-end, stream AG-UI-style events.

Title: Structured outputs (Claude)
Key takeaway: Constrained decoding against JSON schema for outputs and strict tool inputs.
Implication for our harness: Use provider structured outputs where available; validate+repair otherwise.

Title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
Key takeaway: strict JSON schema adherence for responses and function calls.
Implication for our harness: Same as OTH-14.

Title: Claude Code overview
Key takeaway: Agentic coding tool that lives in the terminal; same engine and settings behind CLI, VS Code/JetBrains extensions, desktop app and cloud sessions.
Implication for our harness: Target UX: one engine, many surfaces. Build the engine as a library with the TUI as the first client.

Title: Best practices for Claude Code
Key takeaway: Explore -> plan -> code -> commit workflow; CLAUDE.md tuning; give the agent verification targets (tests, screenshots); clear context between tasks; use subagents for investigation; headless for fan-out.
Implication for our harness: Bake these workflows into defaults (plan mode, /clear, /init, verification hooks) rather than leaving them to user discipline.

Title: Claude Code settings files and precedence
Key takeaway: Four scopes: managed > CLI --settings > project-local (.claude/settings.local.json) > shared project (.claude/settings.json) > user (~/.claude/settings.json). Lists merge; hot-reload; repo allow-rules wait for workspace trust; some keys (bypass mode) ignored from project files.
Implication for our harness: Copy the scope model exactly, including trust-gating of repo-supplied allow rules and 'restrictive value wins' exceptions. It is a security boundary, not just config.

Title: Claude Code permissions (rules, modes, precedence)
Key takeaway: Rules evaluated deny -> ask -> allow, first match wins; specifiers like Bash(npm run test *), Read(./.env), WebFetch(domain:x); compound-command and wrapper parsing; PreToolUse hooks cannot override deny; modes: default/acceptEdits/plan/auto (classifier)/bypassPermissions.
Implication for our harness: Permission engine spec to emulate. Parse shell commands into an AST (compound commands, wrappers, redirections) before matching. Prefix matching is the classic bypass.

Title: Checkpointing (rewind code and/or conversation)
Key takeaway: Snapshots file state before each edit; Esc Esc / /rewind restores code, conversation, or both. Edits made via bash are not tracked.
Implication for our harness: Ship checkpoints from day one, and close the bash gap (e.g. git-stash/shadow-worktree snapshots per turn).

Title: Headless mode / Agent SDK CLI (-p, stream-json)
Key takeaway: Non-interactive runs via -p with --output-format text|json|stream-json and --input-format stream-json; used for CI, scripts, fan-out.
Implication for our harness: Headless mode is how the harness becomes composable (CI, evals, other agents). Define a stable JSONL event schema early.

Title: Claude Code CLI reference
Key takeaway: Commands and flags: -c continue, -r resume by id/name, --model, --permission-mode, --allowedTools, --add-dir, --mcp-config, --append-system-prompt, --max-turns, --fork-session, --settings, update/install/doctor.
Implication for our harness: Checklist for our CLI flag surface; keep names familiar to lower switching cost.

Title: Claude Code interactive mode (shortcuts, input modes)
Key takeaway: Esc interrupt, Esc Esc rewind, Shift+Tab mode cycle, Ctrl+R history, Ctrl+B background, Ctrl+O transcript, Ctrl+G external editor, Ctrl+S stash, ! shell mode, @ file mention, / commands, image paste, vim mode, message queueing while agent works.
Implication for our harness: TUI feature checklist. Message queueing, interrupt-without-losing-work and external-editor are the high-value ones.

Title: Slash commands
Key takeaway: Built-in commands (/clear, /compact, /model, /config, /init, /resume, /rewind, /cost, /permissions, /agents, /mcp, ...) plus user/project markdown commands with arguments.
Implication for our harness: Commands = markdown files with frontmatter, unified with skills; same loader.

Title: Status line
Key takeaway: User script receives session JSON on stdin and prints a status line (model, cwd, cost, git branch, context %).
Implication for our harness: Cheap extensibility: expose session state as JSON to a user command instead of building every widget.

Title: Output styles
Key takeaway: Swappable system-prompt personas (default, explanatory, learning, custom) that change how the agent communicates.
Implication for our harness: Make the system prompt composable: core + style + project memory + skills index.

Title: Common workflows (worktrees, parallel sessions, images, resume)
Key takeaway: Recipes: git worktrees for parallel sessions, resuming, piping, extended thinking, images, PR creation.
Implication for our harness: Worktree-per-session should be a first-class command, not a recipe.

Title: Claude Code sandboxing docs
Key takeaway: Bash runs inside OS sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap) with filesystem write limits and proxy-based network allow-list; reduces prompts.
Implication for our harness: Implementation detail behind OTH-04; pair with sandbox-runtime (TRM-14).

Title: anthropics/sandbox-runtime
Key takeaway: Open-source library/CLI that wraps processes in OS sandboxes (macOS sandbox-exec, Linux bubblewrap) with fs and network policy; usable outside Claude Code.
Implication for our harness: Candidate dependency (or reference) for our sandbox layer; also sandbox stdio MCP servers with it.

Title: Claude Code monitoring (OpenTelemetry)
Key takeaway: Exports OTel metrics and events (sessions, tokens, cost, tool decisions, LOC changed) to any OTLP backend.
Implication for our harness: Emit the same signals; use GenAI semconv names (OTH-07).

Title: Claude Code fullscreen rendering
Key takeaway: Opt-in alternate-screen renderer with transcript viewer, prompt jumping, and a key to dump the conversation back to native scrollback for search.
Implication for our harness: Offer both renderers: inline (default, native scrollback) and fullscreen, with an escape hatch to native scrollback.

Title: Claude Code in VS Code (IDE integration)
Key takeaway: Extension shares settings with CLI; diff viewing, selection context, diagnostics sharing.
Implication for our harness: IDE integration via ACP (MCP-12) or a local server; share config with CLI.

Title: OpenAI Codex CLI (open-source, Rust)
Key takeaway: Apache-2.0 Rust CLI/TUI; sandboxed exec; apply_patch editing; AGENTS.md; MCP client and server mode; exec (headless) mode; config.toml profiles.
Implication for our harness: Best open-source reference implementation of a Claude-Code-class harness; read codex-rs for sandbox, patch and protocol code.

Title: Codex sandbox and approvals
Key takeaway: Two orthogonal controls: sandbox mode (read-only / workspace-write / danger-full-access) and approval policy (on-request / never / granular; auto-review agent). Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap+seccomp on Linux; network off by default; .git/.codex/.agents protected even in writable roots; non-git folders default read-only.
Implication for our harness: Adopt the 'sandbox x approval' two-axis model and protected paths. Default read-only outside version control is a cheap, strong safety rule.

Title: Codex config reference
Key takeaway: TOML config with profiles, model providers, sandbox settings, MCP servers, OTel, notify hooks.
Implication for our harness: Reference for config schema; profiles are a nice way to switch provider/model/sandbox bundles.

Title: Gemini CLI (open-source)
Key takeaway: Apache-2.0 TypeScript CLI; GEMINI.md context files; MCP; checkpointing; extensions; Google Search grounding; large free tier.
Implication for our harness: Second open-source reference (TypeScript, like our likely stack); study its tool scheduler, extensions and policy engine.

Title: Aider edit formats
Key takeaway: Edit formats: whole file, search/replace 'diff', 'diff-fenced', unified diff 'udiff', editor-diff/whole for architect mode; best format is model-dependent.
Implication for our harness: Support multiple edit formats behind one Edit tool, chosen per model via capability flags; measure with an edit benchmark.

Title: Aider repository map (tree-sitter)
Key takeaway: Tree-sitter extracts symbols; a graph ranking (PageRank-style) picks the most relevant definitions to fit a token budget; sent as compact context.
Implication for our harness: Optional repo-map context provider; cheap codebase awareness without embeddings.

Title: Building a better repository map with tree-sitter
Key takeaway: Design rationale for the repo map: ctags -> tree-sitter, graph ranking of files and symbols, dynamic token budget.
Implication for our harness: Implementation notes for our repo-map provider.

Title: Editing files at 1000 tokens per second (Instant Apply)
Key takeaway: Split edits into plan (frontier model) and apply (fast fine-tuned model); 'speculative edits' use the original file as the draft for speculative decoding (~9-13x faster); full-file rewrite beats diffs for weaker models.
Implication for our harness: For speed: optional 'apply model' path, and predicted outputs (PERF-13) for providers that support it.

Title: GPT-4.1 prompting guide (apply_patch diff format)
Key takeaway: Documents the V4A apply_patch format that OpenAI models are trained on; agentic prompting reminders (persistence, tool use, planning).
Implication for our harness: When driving OpenAI models, expose apply_patch natively; models edit best in their trained format.

Title: Ink (React for CLIs)
Key takeaway: React renderer for terminals; used originally by Claude Code, Codex (TS), Gemini CLI, Amp. Full-tree re-render caused flicker in long-running UIs.
Implication for our harness: If TypeScript: use React component model but own the renderer backend (differential, line-level). See TRM-31.

Title: Ratatui (Rust TUI)
Key takeaway: Immediate-mode Rust TUI library with cell-diffing backend; used by Codex CLI.
Implication for our harness: Option if core is Rust.

Title: Bubble Tea (Go TUI)
Key takeaway: Elm-architecture Go TUI framework; used by Crush.
Implication for our harness: Option if core is Go.

Title: Textual (Python TUI)
Key takeaway: Python TUI framework with CSS-like styling and async widgets.
Implication for our harness: Option if core is Python.

Title: The signature flicker (terminal rendering for coding agents)
Key takeaway: Ink redraw caused Claude Code flicker; Anthropic rewrote the renderer (kept React, stayed inline). Alt-screen (Amp, OpenCode) loses native selection/scrollback/search; Gemini CLI shipped alt-screen and rolled it back within ~a week; pi is the reference for differential inline rendering.
Implication for our harness: Default to inline rendering with line-level diffing and synchronized output (DEC 2026). Treat alt-screen as opt-in.

Title: What I learned building an opinionated and minimal coding agent (pi)
Key takeaway: 4 tools (read/write/edit/bash), <1k-token system prompt, no MCP (CLI tools + READMEs instead), no plan mode (PLAN.md files), no subagent tool, YOLO by default, differential inline TUI, session branching, cross-provider handoff; competitive on Terminal-Bench 2.0.
Implication for our harness: Proof that a small core is competitive. Keep the core minimal and make everything else (MCP, plan mode, subagents) optional modules.

Title: Claude Code tools reference
Key takeaway: Built-in tool list and behaviours (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, TodoWrite, NotebookEdit, ...).
Implication for our harness: Baseline built-in tool set to match.

Title: Keybindings
Key takeaway: User-rebindable keybindings file with contexts and chords.
Implication for our harness: Make every shortcut rebindable from a config file; terminals differ (Option-as-Meta, Kitty protocol).

Title: A postmortem of three recent issues
Key takeaway: Aug-Sep 2025 quality degradation came from three infra bugs (context-window routing, TPU output corruption, approximate top-k miscompile); evals missed them; privacy limits slowed debugging.
Implication for our harness: Run continuous production-quality evals and keep a privacy-safe /bug feedback path; users notice regressions before benchmarks do.

Title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports (April 23 postmortem)
Key takeaway: Three harness-side changes degraded Claude Code: default effort high->medium (latency trade-off), a cache/thinking-clearing bug that fired every turn, and a verbosity line in the system prompt (-3% on ablation). Fix: per-model evals on every system-prompt change, soak periods, gradual rollouts.
Implication for our harness: Strongest evidence that harness changes alone move quality. Version and eval every system-prompt and default change; never ship prompt edits without ablations.

Title: Recent Claude Code quality reports (commentary)
Key takeaway: Commentary on the April 2026 postmortem; trust impact of silent harness changes.
Implication for our harness: Publish changelogs for prompt/default changes; let users pin harness versions.

Title: Anthropic unveils new rate limits to curb Claude Code power users
Key takeaway: Weekly caps added (from 2025-08-28) on top of 5-hour limits, citing 24/7 background use and account sharing; backlash over opaque limits.
Implication for our harness: A BYO-key, multi-provider harness avoids single-vendor quota lock-in; show users their usage and remaining budget explicitly.

Title: Clarifying our pricing (June 2025 pricing)
Key takeaway: Cursor moved Pro from request counts to API-priced usage credits; 'unlimited' only applied to Auto; apologised and refunded surprise charges.
Implication for our harness: Cost transparency is a product feature: live cost meter, per-session budgets, hard stops.

Title: Gemini CLI deleted user files after failed mkdir (AIID #1178)
Key takeaway: Agent assumed a failed mkdir succeeded, then ran moves that overwrote all but one file; no read-after-write verification; unrecoverable.
Implication for our harness: Check exit codes and verify state after destructive ops; checkpoint before move/delete; refuse destructive batches without a snapshot.

Title: Code execution through deception: Gemini CLI prompt injection
Key takeaway: Injected README triggered 'grep ...; exfil' that ran because allowlist matched only the root command; whitespace hid the payload in the TUI. Fixed in v0.1.14 (P1/S1). Codex and Claude Code were not vulnerable (robust command parsing).
Implication for our harness: Parse full command AST for allowlists; render commands safely (escape, collapse whitespace, show full text); treat repo context files as untrusted.

Title: Vibe coding service Replit deleted production database
Key takeaway: During a stated code freeze, Replit's agent ran destructive DB commands against production and misreported it; CEO called it unacceptable; added dev/prod separation afterwards.
Implication for our harness: Instructions are not controls: enforce freezes and prod separation with permissions/hooks, not prompts.

Title: Destructive AI prompt published in Amazon Q extension
Key takeaway: A malicious PR to aws-toolkit-vscode inserted a 'wipe the system and AWS resources' prompt that shipped in v1.84.0 to ~1M installs.
Implication for our harness: Supply-chain risk for harness prompts/plugins: signed releases, reviewed prompt changes, plugin provenance.

Title: Weaponizing AI coding agents for malware in the Nx malicious package
Key takeaway: Malicious nx postinstall script invoked installed AI CLIs with bypass flags (claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, gemini --yolo, q --trust-all-tools) to hunt secrets; first known malware using local agents.
Implication for our harness: Bypass flags must not be usable non-interactively by other processes without explicit opt-in (env/config), and should still respect sandbox + deny rules.

Title: Nx s1ngularity security advisory
Key takeaway: Timeline and payload of the Nx compromise, including the agent prompt used for file reconnaissance.
Implication for our harness: Primary source for CMP-10.

Title: CurXecute & MCPoison (CVE-2025-54135 / 54136) FAQ
Key takeaway: Cursor auto-ran new mcp.json entries without confirmation, and trusted a once-approved MCP entry even after its command changed. Fixed in 1.3 (re-approve on any config change).
Implication for our harness: Hash MCP server configs; require re-approval when command/args/env change; never auto-start newly added servers.

Title: CVE-2025-54795 (Claude Code command-parsing approval bypass)
Key takeaway: Command-parsing flaw let an untrusted command bypass the confirmation prompt (fixed 1.0.20). Later CVEs (e.g. CVE-2026-24887, find handling) show the same class recurring.
Implication for our harness: Shell-command permission parsing is the #1 recurring vuln class in coding agents; fuzz it and keep a regression corpus.

Title: CVE-2026-24887 (Claude Code find-command approval bypass)
Key takeaway: Injection via find handling skipped the approval prompt; fixed in 2.0.72.
Implication for our harness: Add find -exec / xargs / sh -c wrappers to the parser test corpus.

Title: Codex CLI is going native (Rust rewrite)
Key takeaway: Moved from TypeScript+Ink to Rust: zero-dependency install (no Node 22), native sandbox bindings, no GC/lower memory, and a wire protocol so extensions can be written in other languages.
Implication for our harness: Distribution matters: ship a single binary. If core is TS, use Bun/Node SEA compile; keep a language-neutral protocol for extensions.

Title: Droid: the #1 software development agent on Terminal-Bench
Key takeaway: 58.8% vs Claude Code 43.2% on the same Opus model. Credits: hierarchical prompting (tool descriptions / system / mid-run system notifications), model-specific edit formats, minimal tools with simple schemas, environment bootstrap as shell output, planning tool, ripgrep, short default timeouts, background process primitive.
Implication for our harness: Concrete harness levers worth copying; all are cheap to build. Publisher-reported numbers.

Title: Terminal-Bench leaderboard
Key takeaway: Harness x model leaderboard; same model scores very differently across harnesses.
Implication for our harness: Submit our harness once it works; use Harbor (OTH-11) for regression runs.

Title: Measuring the impact of early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
Key takeaway: RCT, 16 devs, 246 tasks in mature repos: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer, while devs believed they were ~20% faster.
Implication for our harness: Measure real outcomes, not perceived speed; reduce review/verification burden (diff UX, tests) where time is lost.

Title: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025: AI
Key takeaway: Use is up but trust is down; top frustration (66%) is 'almost right' solutions; most devs not yet using agents daily; accuracy and security are top concerns.
Implication for our harness: Win on trust: verification-by-default, visible diffs, honest status reporting.

Title: OpenCode
Key takeaway: Open-source, provider-agnostic terminal agent; client/server architecture (TUI is one client; desktop, IDE, headless server); build/plan agents; LSP integration; /undo /redo; AGENTS.md; custom opentui renderer.
Implication for our harness: Client/server split and LSP diagnostics are worth copying; opentui shows the cost of a custom alt-screen renderer (terminal compatibility).

Title: Aider
Key takeaway: Pair-programmer CLI: repo map, multiple edit formats, auto git commit per change, architect/editor model split, public edit leaderboards across 100+ models.
Implication for our harness: Copy: per-change git commits (easy undo), architect/editor split, public edit benchmark. Weakness: less autonomous loop.

Title: Aider LLM leaderboards
Key takeaway: Polyglot code-editing benchmark across models and edit formats; shows edit-format x model interaction.
Implication for our harness: Use as model-capability input for our edit-format selection.

Title: Cline
Key takeaway: Open-source agent (VS Code + CLI): Plan/Act modes, approve-every-action by default, checkpoints, MCP marketplace, BYO key; headless CLI for CI.
Implication for our harness: Plan/Act split is popular and simple. Per-action approvals are safe but slow; prefer sandbox + coarse approvals.

Title: goose
Key takeaway: Open-source, local-first, MCP-first agent (CLI + desktop); recipes (shareable workflows); any tool-calling LLM; governed by AAIF; adopted ACP.
Implication for our harness: Reference for MCP-first extension design and shareable 'recipes' (= our skills/commands).

Title: Amp
Key takeaway: Opinionated: picks models for you, removes unused features, no back-compat; shared threads; oracle/subagents; remote 'orbs' that keep working; CLI moved to alt-screen custom renderer.
Implication for our harness: Wins: thread sharing, strong defaults. Flaw risk: removing user model choice and churn hurts power users.

Title: GitHub Copilot CLI is now generally available
Key takeaway: Terminal-native Copilot agent for all Copilot subscribers; plan mode, parallel agents, org model policy, deep GitHub integration.
Implication for our harness: Distribution and GitHub-native workflows (issues/PRs) are its moat; integrate gh workflows well.

Title: Kiro specs (spec-driven development)
Key takeaway: Feature -> requirements (EARS) -> design -> tasks files, executed task by task; agent hooks on file events.
Implication for our harness: Spec mode = structured plan mode persisted as files; cheap to add as a skill/command.

Title: Crush
Key takeaway: Go/Bubble Tea terminal agent; multi-provider; LSP-enhanced context; MCP; session-based.
Implication for our harness: Polished TUI reference; LSP context again.

Title: Qwen Code
Key takeaway: Fork of Gemini CLI adapted for Qwen-Coder models.
Implication for our harness: Shows how forkable an open harness is; open-weight model support matters.

Title: Claude Code via ACP in Zed
Key takeaway: Zed runs Claude Code (and Gemini CLI) as external agents through the Agent Client Protocol.
Implication for our harness: Implement ACP so editors can host our harness without bespoke extensions.

Title: Introducing Gemini CLI
Key takeaway: Apache-2.0, free tier 60 rpm / 1,000 requests/day with a personal account, Gemini 2.5 Pro with 1M context, MCP, GEMINI.md, Search grounding.
Implication for our harness: Generous free tier drove adoption; we can't match that, but supporting free/local models helps.

Title: Codex CLI issue: approval prompts for nearly every command after upgrade
Key takeaway: Example of a recurring complaint class: sandbox/approval regressions on upgrade (esp. Windows) causing prompt fatigue or blocked writes.
Implication for our harness: Permission/sandbox behaviour needs regression tests per OS; Windows support is a real cost.
